exposure: Omicron variant dominant COVID-19 pandemic period
cohort: The study included 492 singleton pregnant women who delivered during a prepandemic period (December 2019-February 2020) and an Omicron surging period (December 2021-February 2022), with the population being predominantly Black.
finding: The study found no significant difference in overall pregnancy-related or neonatal outcomes between the prepandemic and Omicron periods in a Black-dominant population, though maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron surge was associated with an increased neonatal intensive care unit admission rate.
mod_finding: No statistically significant difference in cesarean delivery rates was observed between the prepandemic and Omicron cohorts.
gest_age: Gestational age for included deliveries was 20 weeks or more.
